subject: Completely missing level-2 units in BYM model - what to do?

messages.author: 8d7e6559e413a92b
messages.subject: Completely missing level-2 units in BYM model - what to do?
parts:
Hello, 

I am seeking advice on how to deal with completely missing level 2 data in a BYM model. The bigger picture is as follows:

I am using a BYM model to conduct multilevel poststratification (MRP). In case you're not familiar, MRP is a method for obtaining small-area estimates from a larger-area (e.g. national) survey. Briefly, it involves building a model that predicts individual responses from demographic data. This model is then used to estimate response scores for each combination of demographic characteristics (e.g. expected score for female x 20-25 x holds BS x latina). Then, census data is used to post stratify these predictions at the small-area level of interest. 

I am more or less doing this as well as including a BYM error structure in order to obtain county-level estimates. 

Here is my model code, which should hopefully clarify things: 

rls.f2 <- attend_n ~ 1 +  MedianHouseholdIncome_state +
  dDRPct_state + density_state + f(id, model='bym', graph=g) + 
  f(gender, model='iid') +
  f(race, model='iid') + 
  f(age_3lvl, model='iid') +
  f(educ_3lvl, model='iid')

The issue is that I do not have respondents for some counties. I would be very comfortable with their spatial effects being estimated as a function of adjacent counties, however, I am not sure what the best approach for doing this via INLA is. Any thoughts would be greatly appreciated!

Best,
Joe

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Completely missing level-2 units in BYM model - what to do?
parts:
Hi

as far as I understand it, is that you're missing of the the data (not
covariates, that is a different issue). If so, just set these
observations to NA, and there will be no likelihood contribution from
these counties.

Let me know if I have missed the point...

H

messages.author: 8d7e6559e413a92b
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Completely missing level-2 units in BYM model - what to do?
parts:
Hello, 

Thanks for this! I think maybe you did miss the point a little, but mainly because my explanation was convoluted. My issue was that I had not just missing data, but also missing cases. So, there were literally no rows in my data for which I could make predictions. 

I wound up just adding rows for each missing county based on the most likely person in that person as estimated by census data. That gave me complete IVs for each row and just missingness in the response, which I'm now working on imputing. 

Best,
Joe

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Completely missing level-2 units in BYM model - what to do?
parts:
You seem to have found the solution; you need to include a row for each case you want to predict for (or at least make sure that the model includes all the latent variables required for such predictions.

I would be wary of calling it “imputation” though, as that tends to be a frequentist plugin method; in a fully specified Bayesian model, any missing observations behaves just like any other latent variable; it’s integrated out for the likelihood, and the posterior distribution of the predictors are the needed quantities for inferring those missing values.

Finn
